items.prompt: At what temperature does water freeze?
hints: It is the temperature of melting ice.
items.explanation: Water freezes and ice melts at 0 °C.

items.prompt: Which of these is a gas at room temperature?
items.explanation: Oxygen is a gas at room temperature.

items.prompt: Water boils at 100 degrees ___.
hints: The unit begins with the letter c.
The unit is named after a scientist.
items.explanation: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

items.prompt: What do the particles of a gas do?

options.text: They are packed in a regular pattern.
They are far apart and move freely.
They stay close and slide past each other.

hints: There is a lot of space.
items.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move freely.

items.prompt: Which gas is found in the air we breathe out?

options.why: We do not breathe out helium.
We do not breathe out hydrogen.

hints: It is made when things burn.
items.explanation: We breathe out carbon dioxide.

items.prompt: What happens to water when it freezes?

options.text: It shrinks and takes up less space.
It expands and takes up more space.

hints: Think about a bottle of water in a freezer.
items.explanation: Water expands when it freezes, which is why ice takes up more space.

items.prompt: Why does ice float on water?

options.why: Ice floats because it is less dense.

options.text: Ice takes up more space than the same mass of liquid water.
Ice is made of a different substance.

hints: Take the same mass of each.
items.explanation: Ice takes up more space than the same mass of liquid water, so it floats.

items.prompt: Sort each substance into solid, liquid or gas at room temperature.
hints: Think about which ones you can pour.
items.explanation: Iron and salt are solids, water and oil are liquids, and oxygen and nitrogen are gases.

items.prompt: A student dissolves salt in water. What can be said about the salt particles?

options.text: They are destroyed by the water.
They spread out and mix with the water particles.

options.why: Particles do not change into other particles.

items.explanation: In a solution the dissolved particles mix in with the water particles.

items.prompt: Which gas is found in the air as the biggest part?

options.why: There is only a very small amount.

hints: About four fifths of the air.
It is not used for burning.
items.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about four fifths of the air.

items.prompt: Which of these are gases at room temperature?
hints: Some gases are in the air.
Water and sand are not gases.
items.explanation: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are both gases at room temperature.

items.prompt: What is a solvent?

options.why: A solvent is the liquid in a solution.

options.text: a liquid that dissolves other substances

items.explanation: A solvent is a liquid that other substances dissolve in. Water is a good solvent.

items.prompt: A bottle of water is left in the freezer and cracks. What is the best explanation?

options.text: The water shrank and pulled the bottle.
The water expanded as it froze.
The cold made the plastic expand.
options.why: The ice expanded, not the plastic.

hints: Water takes up more space as ice.
items.explanation: Water expands when it freezes, so it pushed on the bottle and cracked it.

items.prompt: Water ___ when it freezes, so ice floats.
items.explanation: Water expands when it freezes.

items.prompt: The temperature of a pan of boiling water is 100 degrees Celsius. A cup of ice water is at 0 degrees Celsius. What is the difference?
hints: Take the smaller from the larger.
The answer is a round number.
items.explanation: 100 − 0 = 100. The difference is 100 degrees Celsius.

items.prompt: Which of these properties of water is unusual?

options.text: It is a liquid at room temperature.
options.why: Many substances are liquids at room temperature.

hints: Most substances shrink when they freeze.
Think about what happens to a bottle in a freezer.
items.explanation: Most substances take up less space as they freeze. Water takes up more.

items.prompt: Why does the water in a puddle slowly disappear on a sunny day even though it is below 100 °C?

options.text: Some water turns into a gas at the surface.
The water soaks into the Sun.

hints: Water particles can escape from the surface.
The water vapour goes into the air.
items.explanation: Water particles escape from the surface and become a gas called water vapour. This is evaporation.

items.prompt: Which statement about gases is correct?

options.text: Gases do not take up space.
options.why: A balloon filled with gas takes up space.

options.text: Many gases are invisible, but they still take up space and have mass.

hints: A balloon is full of gas.
items.explanation: Gases are matter. They take up space and have mass even if we cannot see them.

items.prompt: Sea ice melts at a slightly lower temperature than pure ice. What is the likely reason?
hints: Dissolved substances change melting and freezing points.
items.explanation: Dissolved salt lowers the temperature at which water freezes, so salty ice melts at a slightly lower temperature.

items.prompt: A scientist heats ice. Which sequence of states does the water pass through?

options.why: That is the order when cooling.

items.explanation: Heating takes ice from solid to liquid and then, at 100 °C, to gas.

items.prompt: Which particle model picture matches a gas?

options.text: particles in a tight, regular pattern
particles far apart and moving fast in all directions
particles close together, sliding past each other

hints: The particles move in all directions.
items.explanation: In a gas the particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions.
